The '''Turkish Cup''' ({{langx|tr|Türkiye Kupası}}) is an annual [[association football|football]] cup competition in [[Turkey]], organised by the [[Turkish Football Federation]] since 1962.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Status of Turkish Cup |url=https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=471&ftxtID=13965 |access-date=6 July 2026 |website=Turkish Football Federation (TFF)}}</ref> During a period of sponsorship by [[Fortis Group|Fortis]], the competition was temporarily known as the '''Fortis Turkish Cup''' ({{langx|tr|Fortis Türkiye Kupası|link=no}}). It is currently sponsored by the state-owned bank [[Ziraat Bank|Ziraat Bankası]] and officially called the '''Ziraat Turkish Cup''' ({{langx|tr|Ziraat Türkiye Kupası|link=no}}).<ref>[http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=267&ftxtID=14186 Ziraat Türkiye Kupası'nın yayıncı kuruluşu Turkuvaz Medya oldu] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030727/http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=267&ftxtID=14186 |date=2016-03-04 }} {{in lang|tr}}, accessed {{Start date|2012|08|08|df=y}}</ref>

The tournament has been held under various formats, including a traditional [[single-elimination tournament|knockout competition]] and group stages on an experimental basis. An expanded format was introduced for the [[2012–13 Turkish Cup|2012–13]] season, with a record 156 teams participating. The structure included a [[round-robin tournament|round-robin]] group stage following five knockout rounds, with group winners and runners-up advancing to the semi-finals and final.<ref name=newformat>[http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=267&ftxtID=15914 Türkiye Kupası heyecanını 156 takım yaşayacak] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304134842/http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=267&ftxtID=15914 |date=2016-03-04 }} Turkish Football Federation {{in lang|tr}}, accessed {{Start date|2012|08|08|df=y}}</ref> The current holders of the cup are [[Trabzonspor]].

== Tournament format ==
{{update|section|inaccurate=yes|date=February 2016}}
[[File:Ziraat Türkiye Kupası 2018-2019.jpg|right|thumb|The current design of the trophy, in use since the [[2005 Turkish Cup final|2005 final]]]]

The Turkish Cup currently involves 164 clubs, drawn from the top four tiers of the [[Turkish football league system]] as well as the [[Turkish Regional Amateur League]]. The winner of the competition qualifies for the play-off round of the [[UEFA Europa League]] and also competes in the [[Turkish Super Cup]] against the [[Süper Lig]] champions.

== Trophy and prize money ==
{{unreferenced section|date=February 2016}}
[[File:Fenerbahçe'nin kazandığı TFF 100. Yıl Ziraat Türkiye Kupası.jpg|thumb|Centennial version of the trophy won by Fenerbahçe in the [[2023 Turkish Cup final|2023 final]]]]

The [[Turkish Football Federation]] (TFF) awards the '''Turkish Cup trophy''' (current design pictured) to the winners of the final. Both winners and runners-up receive 50 medals each. Prize money is also distributed, with payments based on reaching a particular round rather than winning matches, except in the final where the runners-up receive less than the champions.

The total prize fund amounts to approximately US$10.5 million. In addition, as a mark of honour, the cup-winning club wears a roundel of the [[Flag of Turkey|Turkish flag]] during the following season.

=== Final ===
* '''Most wins:''' 19  
** Galatasaray (1963, 1964, 1965, 1966, 1973, 1976, 1982, 1985, 1991, 1993, 1996, 1999, 2000, 2005, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019, 2025)  
* '''Most consecutive titles:''' 4  
** Galatasaray (1963, 1964, 1965, 1966)  
* '''Most consecutive appearances:''' 4  
** Galatasaray (1963, 1964, 1965, 1966 – all wins)  
** Trabzonspor (1975, 1976, 1977, 1978 – two wins)  
** Galatasaray (1993, 1994, 1995, 1996 – two wins)  
* '''Most appearances:''' 24  
** Galatasaray (1963, 1964, 1965, 1966, 1969, 1973, 1976, 1980, 1982, 1985, 1991, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1996, 1998, 1999, 2000, 2005, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019, 2025)  
* '''Biggest win:'''  
** [[Gençlerbirliği S.K.|Gençlerbirliği]] 5–0 [[Eskişehirspor]] (1987)  
* '''Most goals in a final:''' 8  
** [[Antalyaspor]] 3–5 Galatasaray (2000)  
* '''Most goals by a losing side:''' 3  
** Antalyaspor 3–5 Galatasaray (2000)  
* '''Most defeats in a final:''' 11  
** Fenerbahçe (1963, 1965, 1989, 1996, 2001, 2005, 2006, 2009, 2010, 2016, 2018)  

=== Unbeaten ===
* '''Longest unbeaten run:''' 26 matches  
** Galatasaray, 1962–63 to 1966–67 (ended in the quarter-finals, second leg vs [[Altay S.K.|Altay]])  

=== Scorelines ===
* '''Biggest home win:'''  
** 14–2, [[Körfez İskenderunspor|İskenderun Demir Çelikspor]] vs [[Fidan Gençlik S.K.]], Round 2, 1980–81  
* '''Biggest away win:'''  
** 1–10, [[Uşak Sportif|Uşak Belediyespor]] vs [[Sarayköy 1926 FK|Denizli B.S.K.]], Second round, 2012–13
